newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to appeal Swiss ruling on Marcos money.
newsitem.headline: Manila to appeal Swiss ruling on Marcos money.

text.p: The Philippine government said on Wednesday a reported Zurich court ruling blocking the transfer to Manila of $500 million in assets of Ferdinand Marcos in Swiss banks was a temporary setback and it would appeal the verdict.
The Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) said it had ordered its lawyer in Switzerland, Martin Kurer, to elevate the case to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court.

The PCGG issued the statement following press reports from Switzerland saying a Zurich court had upheld the appeals by Marcos lawyers and Swiss banks against a 1995 decision to put the money into an escrow account in Manila.
The 1995 ruling was issued by Zurich district attorney Peter Cosandey.

"The decision of the Zurich court of appeals merely delays the PCGG timetable," said the PCGG, the government agency charged with recovering alleged ill-gained assets of the late Philippine president and his associates.
"However, the government is confident that the Swiss Federal Supreme Court will reverse said decision," it added.
President Fidel Ramos told reporters he was awaiting an official report from the PCGG on the matter.
He said he had directed PCGG chairman Magtanggol Gunigundo "to see me with a proposed plan of action in all aspects...not later than Friday."
Manila claims the deposits in two Swiss banks were part of about $5 billion it said the Marcoses looted from the economy during Marcos's 20-year rule. The family denies the accusation.

Victims of human rights abuses during the Marcos rule have also laid claim to the Swiss-held assets in line with a decision by a jury in Hawaii in 1994 awarding them $1.9 billion in damages for the ordeals they suffered.
Marcos was overthrown in a 1986 popular revolt and died in exile in Hawaii three years later.
